title: Hey, been working on a rules engine to help AI referee rules-heavy TTRPG systems. Could use some alpha testing and feedback.
author: platemaildotgg
selftext:
I've been building this for a few months and it's at the point where it needs people other than me  
in it. It runs in a browser, and it's very much an alpha.

The short version:  
it's a 3.5-Core D&D inspired dungeon crawl, with an AI DM who actually has and follows the rules as they are in the book. Now that the engine is built, essentially any kind of RPG is within reach, the AI should be able to handle it. We started with 3.5 to try and make sure we could get one of the harder systems in terms of rules down first.

**---**

Most AI dungeon masters are improvisers with a rulebook somewhere in the room. They'll tell you the goblin hits, and the number it hit with is whatever seemed right. That's fine for a certain kind of  
play and it is not the kind I wanted. I wanted the number crunch, and I found that AI DM's couldn't  
really deliver it.

What I did was pretty simple at first, start automating various scripts and hooks to force the AI to  
have certain procedures there in context when outputting the next turn. As the project continued,  
the results continued to improve, and it became more and more clear to me that an AI could potentially  
DM 3.5 about as well as a random human DM, with about random human DM level of rules mistakes.

The main engineering problem became the tendency of models to give away information the player doesn't  
have access to, giving away stats, ambushes, and removing difficulty from the game by not respecting  
the fog of war. We ended up putting a two layer system in which the AI's output itself is swept for leaks  
and spoilers before it goes to the player. This helped a lot, though we're still testing.

**---**

**## It's just an Alpha rn**

What's in it right now: six classes, five races, rules to fifth level, and one ruined watchtower in a  
marsh scoped for levels one to three. Full OGL v1.0a ships with the ruleset and is on the site.  
I have another dungeon nearly ready to deploy, and I can't develop much further unless I get some feedback  
and bug reports. I'm inviting anyone who has the time and inclination to give it a shot.

We support two AI providers at the moment, OpenAI and Claude, and the game requires an API key to play  
which basically boils down to needing to make an account with OpenAI or Claude, throw 5 dollar on it (at 5 cents a turn,  
this is all you'll need). Then, put the key in your browser at Platemail.GG. Key never leaves your browser, my site doesn't  
keep it. Essentially BYOAI, though I might be able to finetune a model specifically for this task if there's  
any interest or need for it.

If you're looking for some AI dungeoncrawling that's focused on getting the rules right, I encourage you to give it a shot.
